title: Add signing trust store + basic key rollover support for offline bundles
author: Ethan Park
description: Context: Redwood Private offline bundles will be cryptographically signed and must be verifiable in air-gapped installs. We need a trust model that supports (a) multiple trusted signing keys (during rotation) and (b) a predictable way for customers to update trust roots in offline environments without rebuilding the installer. This PR introduces a local trust store mechanism and implements basic key rollover support in the bundle verification path. Summary of changes: (1) Adds a trust store file format (JSON) that can contain multiple trusted public keys, each with a stable key_id (kid), algorithm, and optional metadata (created_at, not_before, not_after, comment). (2) Installer can load trust store keys from: default embedded trust store (compiled into the binary) OR an operator-provided trust store path (air-gapped friendly) OR an OS-level path (/etc/redwood-private/trust/signing-truststore.json) if present. Precedence: explicit CLI flag > env var > OS path > embedded. (3) Signature verification now selects the verification key by kid when present in the signature envelope; if kid is absent (migration case), we attempt verification against all trusted keys and require exactly one match (fail closed if 0 or >1 match). (4) Key rollover behavior: trust store supports multiple active keys simultaneously. Installer logs which kid was used, and emits a warning if the matched key is marked as "deprecated" in the trust store metadata (non-blocking; intended to help customers notice rotation lag). (5) Adds clear failure modes and remediation hints: unknown kid, empty trust store, malformed key material, and "multiple keys verify" ambiguity (points to duplicated keys / incorrect trust store content). (6) Adds unit tests covering trust store parsing, precedence rules, kid-based selection, and multi-key verification behavior. Notes / non-goals: This PR does not implement key revocation distribution, certificate chains, or customer-managed custom roots (future work tracked separately). It also intentionally does not add network fetches for trust material; offline installs must not depend on outbound connectivity. Follow-ups: docs PR to describe how to update the trust store in air-gapped environments and how rotation will be communicated; integration tests for tampered trust store file will land with the broader verification suite. Risk: low/medium. Changes are gated behind the offline bundle verification code path and default behavior remains "embedded trust store only" unless an operator configures overrides. Tested: unit tests; manual verification with two generated ed25519 keys and a signed manifest; confirmed fail-closed on unknown kid and on empty trust store.
commits: installer/verify: introduce TrustStore loader + precedence rules
signing: add key_id (kid) selection and multi-key verify fallback
tests: trust store parsing and rollover scenarios
docs(dev): update internal README for trust store usage
review_conversation:
Marcus Lin: Can we guarantee we never accept an unpinned key when kid is missing? I want to avoid a scenario where multiple keys verify and we pick the first one.
Ethan Park: Yes. When kid is absent, we try all keys and require exactly one to verify; otherwise we fail with SIGNATURE_AMBIGUOUS and include remediation guidance.

Hanae Suzuki: Where does the embedded trust store come from and how do we update it for a hotfix? Also, can customers provide their own trust store without rebuilding the binary?
Ethan Park: Embedded trust store is a checked-in JSON blob updated as part of the release train. Customers can drop a trust store file into /etc/redwood-private/trust or point the installer at a path via --trust-store; no binary rebuild required.

Connor O'Brien: Please add a note on precedence order and ensure we log the resolved trust store path (but not key material).
Ethan Park: Added an info log: trust_store_source=(flag|env|os|embedded) and trust_store_path when applicable; key bytes never logged.

Owen Phillips: For support, can we surface the kid used in the logs? This will help with 'unknown key after rotation' tickets.
Ethan Park: Added kid to the verification summary line and included it in the preflight report output (without printing full public key).

Marcus Lin (request changes): Add a guard to fail if trust store contains duplicate kids.
Ethan Park: Implemented duplicate kid detection during load; now fails with TRUST_STORE_DUPLICATE_KID and lists the kid values.
release_notes: Installer now supports a local signing trust store with multiple trusted public keys (enables signing key rotation for offline bundles).

Operators can provide a trust store path via --trust-store or REDWOOD_TRUST_STORE_PATH; otherwise installer uses /etc/redwood-private/trust/signing-truststore.json if present, falling back to embedded keys.
Verification fails closed on unknown signing key ids (kid) and on ambiguous multi-key verification.
